chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, from Ibrahim ibn Maimun, from Mus'ab, from Sa'd, from al-Asbagh, from Ali (peace be upon him)
Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: "And they said: Our Lord, Allah, hasten for us our share before the Day of Reckoning." He said: Their share of the torment.
ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'hasten for us our share' mean in Surah Sad?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam Ali (AS) elucidates the concept of 'share' (qism) in Surah Sad, interpreting the disbelievers' plea not as a desire for worldly blessings, but as a demand to hasten their destined portion of divine punishment. This exegesis highlights the Shia scholarly understanding of 'hastening' (ta'jil) as a specific attribute of the wicked who seek immediate retribution rather than patience for reward, reinforcing the theological distinction between the fate of the righteous and the disbelievers.
